title: Baidu Apollo Go robotaxi
summary: The largest paid driverless taxi fleet in China, concentrated in Wuhan.
bodyHtml:
What This Is

Apollo Go operates paid fully driverless rides in Wuhan and several other Chinese cities, with a fleet in the high hundreds and millions of cumulative rides reported. Fares are subsidised and vehicles are concentrated in geofenced districts, so the service is a learning system as much as a business. Cost per vehicle and remote-assistance ratios determine whether it can be run without subsidy.

Status

Attribute Value
Development stage Early commercial
Estimated window 2024–2027
Confidence label Confident
Evidence Editorial synthesis of company, agency and press reporting
Compiled 18 November 2026

Related records

Investment Exposure

China's advantage is deployment volume and permissive local regulators, not a fundamentally different technology stack.

What Would Change The View

  • Rides per vehicle per day.
  • Subsidy per ride and remote-assist cost.
  • Expansion beyond geofenced districts.

Record Notes

Editorial brief, not an imported source note. Named milestones are drawn from company, agency and press reporting; forward dates are announced targets, not verified outcomes. No figure here is an audited statistic.
